- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or shows strong downward momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then drifts back too slowly.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often peaks 1–2 days after true price bottoms.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, reduce forecasted peak by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment shows strong upward momentum but price fails to rise, model overestimates upside; adjust downward by 3–5%.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals without recent sentiment confirmation — model tends to overpredict directionality.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overestimates volatility — cap forecast range within ±3% of recent 7-day average.
